_why: A NAMED STOP is a legitimate halt, but not every legitimate halt needs a
human. On 2026-09-01 the daily cloud-upload lane found the day's YouTube
allowance already spent, printed a stop whose own unblock text read
'Nothing to do; the allowance resets at midnight Pacific and this lane
runs daily' - and then exited 3, failing the job and opening an issue. A
daily lane that exhausts a daily quota does that EVERY day, so the one
notification channel the loop has was spent on the outcome that needs
nobody. This file is the taxonomy that separates the two.
DEFAULT IS needs_human. A code absent from self_resolving stays exit 3.
That is deliberate: forgetting to classify a stop leaves it loud, never
A self-resolving stop still writes loop/state/stops/, still prints the
full NAMED STOP banner, and still appends to the Actions job summary. The
only thing it does not do is fail the job and page the owner.

QUOTA_EXHAUSTED.why: The YouTube allowance resets at midnight Pacific and every lane that raises this runs at least daily, so the work is deferred by a few hours, not lost.
QUOTA_EXHAUSTED.escalation: Three runs in a row means the day's allowance is structurally short, not momentarily spent - the lanes are asking for more units than a day holds. That needs a human: reduce a lane's per-run limit, or spread the caption backfill wider.
